quotes_used_verbatim: A pool lift must remain in place and be operational during all times that the pool is open to guests.
require equal and independent access for people with disabilities for all covered facilities
primary_sources.scope_verified: Fetched specifically to check scope. The document applies to hotels and motels, health clubs, recreation centers, public country clubs and other businesses with swimming pools. VERIFIED: it does not mention cruise ships at all. The article states this explicitly rather than implying the rule binds ships.

claims.legal_restraint: The article deliberately does NOT assert that ADA pool-lift provisions are enforceable against foreign-flagged cruise ships. It states plainly that this is a separate legal question involving maritime jurisdiction which we have not resolved and will not pretend to have resolved. No case law is cited, because none was verified in session.
claims.lived_observation: One sailing, August 2026: no pool or hot tub lift seen deployed at any point; told they exist aboard; a wheelchair user aboard was satisfied with his accommodations and does not swim or use hot tubs - printed precisely because his satisfaction is NOT evidence on the lift question. Prior-sailings advance-notice pattern attributed to our experience of one line, not asserted as policy.
claims.honest_limit_in_body: The article states in its own text: one ship, one week, one deck watched, plus prior sailings on one line - an observation, not a survey. A closing section lists explicitly what we do not know and invites correction with attribution.
claims.not_claimed: No claim about which specific ships have permanent lifts; no fleet-wide or industry-wide finding; no claim about any line's written accessibility policy; no notice-period figure stated as policy.

pastoral_handling: Names the dignity cost of advance-notice regimes (being asked to schedule leisure with a precision nobody else on the deck is asked for) without catastrophising, and credits the satisfied wheelchair user's experience as genuine rather than using him as a prop.
